user_query: My boss refuses to pay me for overtime work.
variations: I worked extra hours but got no money
Company says no overtime pay for my role
Claiming money for working weekends and public holidays
part_a_general_info: Under Part 4 of the Employment Act 1968, overtime (OT) pay is mandatory only for: (a) workmen (manual labour) earning up to $4,500/month, and (b) non-workmen earning up to $2,600/month. For these employees, OT must be paid at 1.5 times the hourly basic rate of pay. Managers and executives are generally not covered under Part 4 and their entitlement to OT depends strictly on their employment contract.
triage_questions: Q1: What is your job role (e.g., manual worker, clerk, manager)?
Q2: What is your basic monthly salary?
Q3: Does your employment contract specifically mention overtime pay?
Q4: Are you a Singapore Citizen/PR or Work Permit holder?
branching_logic: If Q1 = Manager OR Q2 > $2,600 (non-workman) → Statutory OT likely does not apply; depends on contract.
If Q4 = Work Permit → Route to MOM/TADM with language support if needed.
routing: Route A (Covered under Part 4): File claim at TADM.
Route B (Not covered, contract silent): Statutory claim unlikely to succeed. Refer to PBSG Employment Clinic for contract review if amount is substantial.
Route C (Not covered, contract provides OT): File claim at TADM for breach of contract.
guardrail: Must NOT calculate the specific OT sum owed or interpret ambiguous contract clauses.
